messages.content:
You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Salt Reed broadcast","question":"What claims can the archivist put in the tape catalogue?","claims":{"A":"Staff digitised the master tape on Friday.","B":"The original tape casing is labelled programme SR-63.","C":"The master tape contains more than 30 minutes of programme audio."},"handoff":"The archivist can confidently include claim A that staff digitised the master tape on Friday, supported by the transfer log (S1). Claim B should not be included, as the original tape casing is labeled SR-36, contradicting the claim it is SR-63 (S3). Claim C remains uncertain; while the programme grid allocates 35 minutes, this is only an estimate and engineers often removed content from masters, so the master tape’s actual audio length is unclear. Therefore, only claim A is reliably supported for the tape catalogue.","follow_up":{"S4":"independent digital preservation report distinguishes programme audio from silence and assigns the master 32 minutes of programme audio."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"supported","citations":["S1"],"confidence":95},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S3"],"confidence":90},"C":{"status":"supported","citations":["S4"],"confidence":85}},"note":"Claim A is decisively supported by the transfer log (S1) confirming digitisation on Friday. Claim B is contradicted by the tape casing label (S3) showing SR-36, not SR-63. Claim C was initially unresolved due to uncertainty about actual audio length, but the independent digital preservation report (S4) provides strong evidence of 32 minutes of programme audio, supporting the claim with moderate confidence."}

parsed.note: Claim A is decisively supported by the transfer log (S1) confirming digitisation on Friday. Claim B is contradicted by the tape casing label (S3) showing SR-36, not SR-63. Claim C was initially unresolved due to uncertainty about actual audio length, but the independent digital preservation report (S4) provides strong evidence of 32 minutes of programme audio, supporting the claim with moderate confidence.
